Title: A microscope with a noisy ruler
Mental picture: Zooming in reveals a curve’s local slope, but eventually the measuring marks become too coarse for the remaining difference. The useful magnification balances geometric detail against measurement noise.
Shared structure: Finite differences approximate a derivative with truncation error, while subtraction and division amplify finite-precision errors.
Limits: This picture assumes the model for evaluation error and sufficient smoothness; exact arithmetic has no rounding floor, and noisy data may obey a different error law.
Transfer question: What changes if halving the sampling distance doubles the noise contribution?

Title: Distances on a stretched rubber map
Mental picture: Imagine transferring a small circle through a rubber map: it may become a very thin ellipse. Undoing the map requires large corrections in its compressed direction.
Shared structure: Singular values measure directional stretching; the ratio of largest to smallest stretching controls relative sensitivity of an invertible linear solve.
Limits: Conditioning concerns the problem, not the quality of a particular algorithm. The geometric explanation uses the Euclidean norm; other norms have different unit balls.
Transfer question: Which direction could hide a large solution error behind a small residual?
Patterns: Geometry and distance; Change of coordinates

Title: A repair receipt for a computed answer
Mental picture: A mechanic hands back an answer together with a receipt showing how much the original specification had to change to make that answer exact. A tiny repair can still change the outcome greatly when the specification is sensitive.
Shared structure: Backward error measures a perturbation to the input problem; forward error measures the resulting output discrepancy, linked through conditioning.
Limits: A small backward error does not guarantee a small forward error for an ill-conditioned system. The perturbation model must specify which inputs may change.
Transfer question: Can the computed answer be exact for a nearby problem even when it is far from the intended answer?

Title: Narrowing a search strip
Mental picture: Two markers bracket a crossing. Inspect the middle, keep the half still containing a crossing, and repeat until the search strip is short enough.
Shared structure: A sign-changing interval invariant is preserved while its length decreases geometrically.
Limits: Continuity and opposite endpoint signs are essential. A narrow bracket identifies at least one root, but it does not establish that there is only one root inside.
Transfer question: What invariant lets an iterative search discard half its candidates safely?

Title: Canceling a known blur
Mental picture: Take two measurements whose blur follows the same predictable rule at different scales. A weighted subtraction can cancel the leading blur without knowing the true value.
Shared structure: Richardson extrapolation eliminates a leading error coefficient by combining two asymptotic approximations.
Limits: Cancellation only works when the assumed asymptotic error expansion applies; singularities and rounding can defeat it. Negative weights mean this is not an ordinary positive average.
Transfer question: Which error term is shared across two approximations, and can its coefficient be eliminated?

Title: Choosing where to place sensors
Mental picture: Sensors placed at convenient equal distances can leave a reconstructed curve wobbling badly near its ends. Moving the sensors toward the ends can make the reconstruction less sensitive.
Shared structure: Interpolation-node geometry controls the norm of the reconstruction operator and amplification of data errors.
Limits: Interpolation is exact at the chosen nodes but may still fail between them. Noise, smoothness, polynomial degree and alternative approximation spaces all matter.
Transfer question: How does the placement of information affect the reliability of the reconstructed whole?

Title: A flexible ruler through fixed pegs
Mental picture: Bend a thin ruler through several pegs and let it settle into the least-bent shape. Smoothness between the pegs is selected by an energy cost, not specified point by point.
Shared structure: A natural cubic spline interpolates the data while minimizing the squared second-derivative integral over the appropriate H2 class.
Limits: A real ruler has thickness, material and nonlinear geometry; the analogy uses a small-deflection quadratic bending model. Different endpoint constraints produce different splines.
Transfer question: Which measure of roughness would select a useful interpolant for your data?

Title: A few strategically placed weighing stations
Mental picture: Instead of weighing every point along a road, place a few stations where their weighted readings reproduce an entire family of test loads exactly. Orthogonality tells you where those stations should sit.
Shared structure: Gaussian quadrature chooses nodes and weights to match integration on polynomials through degree 2n−1.
Limits: Exactness is for a prescribed polynomial family and weight, not every function. Singular or highly oscillatory integrands may need transformations or different quadrature rules.
Transfer question: Which family of test functions should a finite measurement scheme reproduce exactly?

Title: Aligning a vector with a folding mirror
Mental picture: A mirror can redirect a vector onto a coordinate axis without changing lengths. Repeating carefully chosen reflections untangles matrix columns into a triangular arrangement.
Shared structure: Orthogonal Householder transformations preserve Euclidean geometry while zeroing selected coordinates.
Limits: A reflection is a linear operation about a hyperplane through the origin. Floating-point implementations still require stable sign choices and accumulate small errors.
Transfer question: Can a calculation be simplified by transformations that preserve the geometry you care about?

Title: Exploring a building one corridor at a time
Mental picture: You cannot survey a huge building at once, but each step shows what the same movement rule does to a newly discovered direction. Keep a compact map of the explored part and solve your problem there.
Shared structure: Krylov methods build polynomial images of one starting vector and project a large linear problem into that growing space.
Limits: A larger explored space does not guarantee fast convergence; nonnormality, spectrum and restarting matter. Orthogonality can degrade in finite precision.
Transfer question: What useful subspace can you build when you can apply an operator but cannot inspect all its entries?

Title: A calculation with fast and slow clocks
Mental picture: A system contains a fast relaxation that has almost vanished and a slow motion you still care about. An explicit clock may be forced to tick at the fast scale even though the visible behavior changes slowly.
Shared structure: Stiffness separates stability-limited step size from the time scale needed for accuracy in the solution of interest.
Limits: Stability permits a step; it does not make that step accurate. Nonlinear solves and nonnormal systems add complications beyond a single decay rate.
Transfer question: Is your step size limited by visible accuracy or by a rapidly decaying mode?
Patterns: Scaling and homogeneity; Exponentials and logarithms

Title: Reading from upstream on a conveyor belt
Mental picture: Objects arriving at a point came from the upstream side of a conveyor. A discrete prediction should sample from that side and allow information to cross no more cells than its update can represent.
Shared structure: Upwind differencing matches the sign of characteristic velocity, while a CFL bound aligns numerical and physical dependence domains.
Limits: The conveyor picture is for simple advection. The upwind method adds numerical diffusion; the CFL condition is generally necessary, not a universal sufficient stability test.
Transfer question: From which direction does the information needed at this point arrive?
Patterns: Geometry and distance; Conservation and balance

Title: A trampoline described by a few allowed shapes
Mental picture: A continuous sheet has infinitely many possible shapes. Restrict it to shapes your mesh can express, then find the one balancing load and elastic energy within that restricted family.
Shared structure: Galerkin projection restricts a variational equation to a finite-dimensional trial space; coercivity controls the error relative to best approximation.
Limits: The PDE energy here is a simplified model. Céa’s estimate requires a continuous coercive bilinear form and conforming spaces; it does not cover every discretization.
Transfer question: Is the main error caused by the solver or by the shapes your approximation space excludes?

Title: Extending an assembly line between stations
Mental picture: A factorial machine multiplies by the next integer at each station. An integral supplies a smooth extension between stations while keeping the same stepping rule.
Shared structure: The gamma integral satisfies a shift recurrence and takes factorial values at positive integers.
Limits: A recurrence plus integer values alone does not uniquely specify a continuous extension. Additional properties such as positivity and log-convexity distinguish gamma, and complex arguments introduce poles.
Transfer question: What extra structure is needed when a discrete rule is extended to continuous inputs?

Title: Separating the size of a pie from its shares
Mental picture: Two positive amounts can be described by their total size and the fraction belonging to the first amount. In those coordinates, a joint calculation splits into one integral for size and another for proportion.
Shared structure: The beta–gamma identity follows from a change of variables from positive coordinates to a total and a unit-interval share.
Limits: The probability interpretation needs positive real shape parameters and the appropriate independence setup. The analytic identity itself extends to complex parameters without literal pie shares.
Transfer question: Would separating total magnitude from relative composition factor your problem?

Title: Choosing an instrument’s natural notes
Mental picture: A sound can be expanded in pure notes, but different instruments suggest different useful note families. Orthogonal polynomials play a similar role when the geometry or weight is not periodic.
Shared structure: Orthogonal systems decompose functions relative to a specified inner product and integration weight.
Limits: These notes need not describe physical frequencies. Orthogonality depends on the chosen weight and domain; completeness is a separate question.
Transfer question: Which inner product makes the natural components of your problem independent?

Title: An uneven clock around a circle
Mental picture: Keep the circular geometry but let the clock slow down and speed up with position. Inverting the accumulated travel time gives a new family of sine-like coordinates.
Shared structure: Elliptic amplitude is an inverse integral; Jacobi functions preserve a trigonometric identity while changing the relation between phase and time.
Limits: The clock is a mathematical parameterization, not necessarily physical time. The modulus convention matters; k and m=k² must not be confused.
Transfer question: Can a nonlinear motion become simple geometry viewed through a different clock?

Title: A map whose distances measure zoom
Mental picture: On an ordinary ruler, equal steps add the same amount. On a logarithmic ruler, equal steps multiply by the same factor, making repeated zooms look like translations.
Shared structure: The substitution x=e^u converts multiplicative scaling into addition and relates Mellin analysis to Fourier analysis.
Limits: The coordinate change introduces a weight and a convergence strip; Mellin and Fourier transforms are not interchangeable without those factors.
Transfer question: Is your problem organized by differences or by ratios?
Patterns: Scaling and homogeneity; Change of coordinates

Title: A grid seen in position and frequency
Mental picture: A regular arrangement of locations has a corresponding regular arrangement of frequencies. A Gaussian makes the trade particularly clear: narrowing its spatial profile broadens its frequency profile.
Shared structure: Poisson summation exchanges spatial lattice sums with Fourier lattice sums, producing theta scale inversion for a Gaussian.
Limits: Normalization constants depend on the Fourier convention. Poisson summation requires regularity and decay; arbitrary unsummable lattice values cannot be exchanged formally.
Transfer question: Can an expensive sum become rapidly convergent after moving to reciprocal scale?

Title: A ledger with separate credits and debits
Mental picture: A net balance can be small even when large amounts moved in both directions. Keep separate nonnegative credit and debit columns to measure the full activity.
Shared structure: Jordan decompositions split signed objects into monotone or positive components, while total variation records absolute accumulated change.
Limits: The decompositions have different objects and uniqueness conventions: measure Jordan parts are canonical, while arbitrary increasing-function decompositions need not be.
Transfer question: Could cancellation be hiding a large amount of underlying variation?

Title: A budget that forbids hidden spikes
Mental picture: A landscape can look almost flat everywhere you inspect while storing substantial mass in increasingly narrow spikes. A uniform tail budget prevents that mass from disappearing from view.
Shared structure: Uniform integrability controls concentration of integral mass, allowing convergence in measure to upgrade to L1 convergence on finite measure spaces.
Limits: Small exceptional sets alone are insufficient. The stated equivalence uses a finite measure space; infinite spaces also require control of mass escaping to infinity.
Transfer question: Where could mass hide while pointwise or measure-based checks appear successful?

Title: Uniform travel after excluding a few roads
Mental picture: Travel times improve point by point across a region, but the slowest road may keep moving. Excluding a region of arbitrarily small size can make the improvement uniform on everything left.
Shared structure: Egorov’s theorem trades a small exceptional set for uniform convergence of an almost-everywhere convergent sequence on a finite measure space.
Limits: The discarded set can depend on the allowed size, and finite total measure is essential. The theorem does not say the original convergence was uniform.
Transfer question: Would removing a quantitatively small exceptional region turn local control into global control?

Title: Recognizing an object from all its shadows
Mental picture: Instead of measuring an object directly, inspect the readings cast onto every allowed linear sensor. Convergence of each reading can occur even when the objects remain far apart in norm.
Shared structure: Weak convergence is convergence under every continuous linear functional, a weaker demand than norm convergence.
Limits: The collection of all sensors is crucial; checking a few is not enough. Weak convergence and coordinatewise convergence coincide only under additional structure and boundedness.
Transfer question: Which observables need to converge for the question you actually care about?

Title: A compact console of bounded sensors
Mental picture: Imagine a collection of measuring devices whose readings are uniformly bounded on every input. If we judge devices only by their readings on individual inputs, the whole bounded collection has a compact closure.
Shared structure: Banach–Alaoglu gives weak-star compactness of the dual unit ball; the topology is pointwise evaluation on the original space.
Limits: Compactness need not mean every sequence has a convergent subsequence unless metrizability conditions such as separability are available. Compactness changes with the topology.
Transfer question: What topology makes bounded sets compact while preserving the measurements you need?

Title: Quality control for an inverse machine
Mental picture: A machine transforms one kind of input into another without losing or duplicating outputs. In complete normed spaces, bounded linear operation forces the reverse machine to be bounded too.
Shared structure: The bounded inverse theorem uses completeness and bijective linearity to convert algebraic invertibility into continuous invertibility.
Limits: The guarantee can fail for incomplete spaces or for an inverse defined only on a nonclosed range. Boundedness does not imply a numerically small condition number.
Transfer question: Which completeness or closed-range assumption makes an inverse operation stable as a map?

Title: A keyboard whose high keys fade
Mental picture: Pressing any key is allowed, but the machine attenuates higher keys more and more. Its outputs can be approximated by retaining only finitely many effective directions.
Shared structure: A compact self-adjoint operator admits eigenmodes with nonzero eigenvalues tending to zero; finite spectral truncations approximate it in operator norm.
Limits: General compact operators need not have an orthogonal eigenbasis. Eigenvalues may be negative in the self-adjoint case, and an infinite-dimensional kernel must be included.
Transfer question: Which directions have so little effect that they can be omitted to a controlled tolerance?

Title: Gatekeepers for an equation
Mental picture: Some right-hand sides cannot pass through a linear machine because they conflict with quantities detected by the reverse machine’s null sensors. Orthogonality to those sensors is the admission rule.
Shared structure: Fredholm solvability connects the range of I−K to the kernel of its Hilbert adjoint when K is compact.
Limits: The exact range characterization and finite-dimensional obstructions require the Fredholm hypotheses. For arbitrary operators, the range may be nonclosed and orthogonality characterizes only its closure.
Transfer question: Which linear measurements must vanish before the equation can have a solution?

Title: Controlling wrinkles by controlling strain
Mental picture: A fabric cannot form arbitrary sharp wrinkles if enough of its local strain is bounded in aggregate. How much smoothness follows depends on the space dimension and the strength of the bound.
Shared structure: Sobolev and Morrey inequalities convert integrability of weak derivatives into integrability or Hölder control of the function.
Limits: The analogy does not promise smoothness from every derivative norm. Critical exponents, dimension, boundary conditions and representative choices matter.
Transfer question: Is your derivative budget above, below or at the dimension-dependent regularity threshold?
Patterns: Scaling and homogeneity; Geometry and distance

Title: A border checkpoint for an interior field
Mental picture: An interior description does not automatically say what happens exactly at the border. A trace operator supplies the boundary information that survives the interior norm.
Shared structure: Sobolev traces extend restriction to the boundary continuously from smooth functions to suitable weakly differentiable functions.
Limits: Pointwise restriction is not meaningful for arbitrary equivalence classes of measurable functions. Domain regularity and the correct boundary function space are part of the theorem.
Transfer question: What notion of boundary data is justified by the regularity you actually have?
Patterns: Boundary and interior; Limits and convergence

Title: A point tap recorded by test instruments
Mental picture: An ideal tap at one point has no ordinary density spread over a region. Instead, describe its effect on every smooth measuring profile; each device reports its value at the tap location.
Shared structure: The Dirac distribution is a linear functional on test functions, and jumps produce Dirac masses under distributional differentiation.
Limits: The delta is not an ordinary function with an infinite point value. Products of arbitrary distributions are generally undefined, despite useful formal notation.
Transfer question: Can an object be defined more cleanly by how it acts on probes than by pointwise values?

Title: An adjustable frosted-glass window
Mental picture: Viewing a rough picture through a small blur makes its features smooth. Reducing the blur can recover the original picture in an appropriate sense while each blurred version remains easier to differentiate.
Shared structure: Mollification convolves with scaled smooth kernels; convergence depends on the original function space or distribution topology.
Limits: A blur does not recover pointwise values everywhere or invert lost information stably. Near a domain boundary, extension or restriction to smaller subdomains is needed.
Transfer question: Which properties survive smoothing, and in which topology can you remove the blur?

Title: An odometer counting turns around a hole
Mental picture: Walk a closed path while tracking the direction to a fixed point. The total accumulated turn is an integer, and a logarithm can return to its starting value only when the relevant winding obstruction vanishes.
Shared structure: The integral of dz/(z−a) measures winding; nonzero winding obstructs a globally single-valued logarithm around a hole.
Limits: A path may self-intersect, and the count is signed. The obstruction concerns the image of the function or the chosen puncture, not merely whether a drawing looks complicated.
Transfer question: Which closed-loop measurement could obstruct defining a single-valued potential?
Patterns: Boundary and interior; Symmetry and invariance

Title: Building an entire function from a zero blueprint
Mental picture: A blueprint marks where a function must vanish and how many times. Infinite construction needs compensating factors so the accumulated product settles down instead of diverging.
Shared structure: Weierstrass products prescribe zeros of an entire function; exponential factors manage convergence and represent zero-free freedom.
Limits: Zeros alone do not determine an entire function: multiplication by exp(g) preserves all zeros. Infinite products require convergence controls and cannot be manipulated like finite products blindly.
Transfer question: What information beyond the zeros is needed to identify a function uniquely?

Title: Reconstructing a room from its boundary microphones
Mental picture: For special fields, readings around the room’s boundary determine every interior value. The reconstruction weights each boundary location differently depending on the interior point.
Shared structure: Integral representation formulas reconstruct harmonic or holomorphic fields from boundary data using kernels.
Limits: Arbitrary interior fields are not determined this way; harmonicity or holomorphicity is essential. Cauchy’s complex kernel is not a probability weight, while the Poisson kernel is positive and normalized.
Transfer question: Which governing equation makes boundary information sufficient for reconstruction?

Title: A map that preserves tiny crossing angles
Mental picture: A flexible map can reshape a simply connected region into a disk while preserving infinitesimal angles. Euclidean distances change, but a different disk distance reveals a useful contraction principle.
Shared structure: Conformal maps preserve angles locally; disk holomorphic maps contract the pseudohyperbolic metric, with automorphisms as exact isometries.
Limits: Conformality does not preserve Euclidean lengths or areas. The Riemann mapping theorem excludes the whole plane and multiply connected domains, and boundary extension needs additional assumptions.
Transfer question: Would a different geometry make the natural maps of your problem preserve or contract distance?
Patterns: Change of coordinates; Geometry and distance

Title: Patching a hole that carries no singular load
Mental picture: A function may be undefined at one point even though nothing blows up nearby. Bounded holomorphic behavior lets that missing value be filled in without creating a seam.
Shared structure: An isolated bounded holomorphic singularity is removable; the negative Laurent coefficients must vanish.
Limits: Boundedness is sufficient for a complex holomorphic function, not for every merely continuous or real differentiable punctured function. A pole or essential singularity cannot be patched this way.
Transfer question: Is a missing point a genuine obstruction or only a defect in the chosen representation?

Title: A mixing bowl that keeps softening peaks
Mental picture: Repeated local mixing redistributes a profile into weighted averages. Peaks cannot grow under this averaging, and the small-scale features fade fastest.
Shared structure: The positive unit-mass heat kernel contracts Lp norms and damps Laplacian eigenmodes at rates proportional to their eigenvalues.
Limits: Boundary conditions may add or remove total mass; Dirichlet heat flow is not globally mass preserving. Backward heat reconstruction is highly unstable even though forward smoothing is well behaved.
Transfer question: Which features will repeated averaging erase first, and which quantities survive?

Title: An arrival cone for a traveling message
Mental picture: A message traveling at a fixed maximum speed can reach only a widening region as time passes. In three spatial dimensions, the wave formula has the striking form of sampling an expanding shell.
Shared structure: Finite propagation bounds dependence by a cone, and Kirchhoff’s formula expresses the three-dimensional wave solution through spherical means.
Limits: The shell-only feature is dimension dependent; it should not be transferred blindly to two dimensions or to heat flow. The wave equation describes signed amplitudes, not a positive averaging process.
Transfer question: What does the dependence region tell you before you solve the equation?
Patterns: Geometry and distance; Conservation and balance

Title: A catalog of responses to single taps
Mental picture: If a system is linear, record how it reacts to a tap at each location. A distributed input is then handled by combining the catalog entries with the input’s weights.
Shared structure: Green kernels represent inverse differential operators, while translation invariance makes the kernel depend only on position difference and gives convolution.
Limits: A Green kernel depends on the operator and boundary conditions, and may fail to exist without compatibility or normalization. Superposition does not apply to general nonlinear equations.
Transfer question: Can solving one point-response problem replace solving many distributed-source problems?

Title: Finding the one neighborhood that matters
Mental picture: In a sharply weighted sum, most regions contribute almost nothing; in a rapidly oscillating sum, most contributions cancel. The surviving neighborhood can often be understood by a quadratic local model.
Shared structure: Laplace’s method concentrates near a minimum, while stationary phase concentrates near a nondegenerate critical point through cancellation; both produce inverse-square-root scales in one dimension.
Limits: Concentration and cancellation are different mechanisms. Degenerate or multiple critical points, endpoints and coalescing saddles require different powers or combined contributions.
Transfer question: Which region survives the weighting or cancellation, and what local model describes it?

Title: Reassigned voting rights
Mental picture: Imagine a council that gives each member a different number of votes for every question. The council's answer is an average, but the question determines whose view counts most.
Shared structure: A normalized nonnegative set of weights forms a convex combination. Attention chooses these weights from query-key comparisons; conditional expectation uses probabilities appropriate to the information available.
Limits: A neural attention weight is a learned computational coefficient, not necessarily a probability that a person is correct or a faithful explanation of a model's decision. Signed linear combinations fall outside this voting picture.
Transfer question: When a familiar formula looks unlike an average, can its coefficients be normalized into voting weights?

Title: The balanced tray and the leftover tilt
Mental picture: Place weighted objects along a ruler and find the support point that balances the tray. Now imagine making a separate tray for each group of objects.
Shared structure: A squared-error minimizer is a mean. Conditional means minimize squared error within information groups, and the remaining error is orthogonal to every square-integrable function of that information.
Limits: The tray picture uses positive mass and Euclidean squared distance. Conditional expectation need not be linear in the observed variables; the affine formula needs the Gaussian or a suitable special structure.
Transfer question: Which part of a prediction error comes from changing group centers, and which part remains within each group?

Title: Practice sheets and the unseen exam
Mental picture: A student studies a set of practice questions and scores perfectly on them. An unseen exam tests whether the student learned a transferable rule or memorized the sheets.
Shared structure: Empirical risk measures performance on observed examples. Population risk averages over the data law; validation and uniform convergence address the gap caused by selecting a model using the training set.
Limits: Repeatedly tuning on the same validation set makes it part of training. The guarantees require the stated sampling assumptions; an exam drawn from a new distribution may measure a different skill.
Transfer question: Which choices in your workflow have already seen the data you are calling a test set?
Patterns: Averaging; Randomness and distribution; Limits and convergence

Title: A repair shop with a complexity bill
Mental picture: A repair shop can fit a machine perfectly by adding many custom parts. Each part also adds a maintenance bill, so the shop balances fit against upkeep.
Shared structure: Regularization adds a penalty to empirical loss. For a suitable likelihood and prior, this same optimization is maximum a posteriori estimation; the penalty controls which explanations are preferred.
Limits: A mathematical penalty need not equal real maintenance cost, and smaller coefficients do not automatically mean a better model. The MAP equivalence depends on the exact likelihood, scaling and prior.
Transfer question: What preference about possible solutions is your penalty charging for?

Title: Two scales with shared error
Mental picture: Weigh an unknown parcel beside a reference parcel on a slightly drifting scale. Subtracting an appropriately scaled reference reading can remove much of the shared wobble.
Shared structure: A control variate subtracts a centered correlated quantity with known expectation. The optimal coefficient removes a linear projection of the noise without changing the target mean.
Limits: An inaccurately known reference mean introduces bias. Variance reduction is not guaranteed for an arbitrary coefficient, and SVRG's reference quantity must be formed consistently with its objective.
Transfer question: Can you cheaply compute a correlated quantity whose expectation is already known?

Title: Paired weather reports
Mental picture: One weather report deliberately uses a high random input while its paired report uses the matching low input. Their average can be steadier because some overestimation in one offsets underestimation in the other.
Shared structure: The variance of an average contains a covariance term. Antithetic sampling constructs negatively correlated estimates while keeping each marginal distribution correct.
Limits: Complementary inputs do not guarantee negatively correlated outputs for a nonmonotone model. The paired forecasts are intentionally dependent, so independent-sample error formulas cannot be applied blindly.
Transfer question: What transformation preserves your simulation's input law while tending to reverse its output error?
Patterns: Randomness and distribution; Symmetry and invariance; Averaging

Title: A neighborhood poll
Mental picture: To guess a household's preference, ask nearby households rather than the entire city equally. A wider neighborhood brings more answers, but may mix places with different preferences.
Shared structure: Local regression trades sampling variability against smoothing bias by choosing which observations receive weight and how rapidly that weight decreases with distance.
Limits: Geographic closeness is only a picture for a chosen feature-space metric. In high dimensions, nearest points may still be far away, and irrelevant coordinates can dominate distance.
Transfer question: What makes two examples meaningfully close for the quantity you want to predict?
Patterns: Averaging; Geometry and distance; Scaling and homogeneity

Title: Elastic camps and moving flagpoles
Mental picture: Assign each traveler to a camp and stretch a spring from the traveler to that camp's flagpole. Move each flagpole to reduce its camp's total squared stretch, then reassign travelers.
Shared structure: The k-means objective alternates between minimizing assignments and minimizing center locations. For fixed assignments, each optimal center is the arithmetic mean of its assigned vectors.
Limits: Travelers are fixed data points, not moving particles. The procedure can reach a local minimum and needs a rule for empty camps; a decreasing objective does not imply the globally best clustering.
Transfer question: Can your joint optimization be divided into blocks that become simple when the other blocks are fixed?

Title: Soft club memberships
Mental picture: A person may partly belong to several clubs instead of choosing exactly one. Each club updates its profile by counting each person only in proportion to their current membership.
Shared structure: Mixture-model responsibilities are conditional component probabilities. The Gaussian-mixture M-step uses these probabilities as weights for means, covariances and mixture proportions.
Limits: The clubs are latent statistical components, not necessarily real social groups. Gaussian mixture likelihoods can diverge when a component collapses onto a data point; EM's local ascent is not a universal existence guarantee.
Transfer question: If hidden membership were known, would your hard estimation problem reduce to a familiar weighted calculation?

Title: The percentile ruler
Mental picture: Replace a ruler marked in centimeters with one marked by the fraction of people shorter than each mark. Equal steps on the new ruler represent equal probability mass.
Shared structure: A cumulative distribution function maps values to cumulative probability. For a continuous law, this transform produces a uniform variable, and a generalized quantile reverses the process for sampling.
Limits: If the distribution has atoms, ordinary F(X) is not uniform; jumps need a randomized convention for a uniform transform. A quantile function need not be an ordinary two-sided inverse.
Transfer question: Would expressing a variable in probability units reveal a pattern hidden by its physical units?
Patterns: Change of coordinates; Randomness and distribution

Title: Arriving between buses
Mental picture: A passenger arrives at a random time and tends to land inside a long gap between buses. Counting gaps equally and observing time equally therefore tell different stories.
Shared structure: Stationary time sampling weights a renewal interval in proportion to its length. Integrating age across each interval gives the mean residual waiting time, while long-run rewards divide accumulated reward by accumulated time.
Limits: The residual-wait formula needs a stationary renewal setting and a finite second moment. A fixed arrival time synchronized to a timetable is not a random time sample, and Little's law is a separate flow-accounting identity.
Transfer question: Are you sampling events equally, people equally, or units of time equally?

Title: Jars and starting counters
Mental picture: Keep one jar of counters for each category. Observations add counters, while the starting contents express how strongly you want to stabilize estimates before much data arrive.
Shared structure: Dirichlet conjugacy adds observed category counts to prior parameters. The posterior predictive probability is a normalized count, combining prior mass with data mass.
Limits: Dirichlet parameters can be fractional and are not necessarily literal historical observations. A prior is a modeling choice; adding pseudocounts does not repair misspecified categories or biased sampling.
Transfer question: Does your update combine evidence by addition before turning it into a normalized average?

Title: An evidence ledger
Mental picture: A ledger tracks how strongly new evidence favors one explanation over another. Multiplicative evidence factors become additive entries when the accountant switches to logarithms.
Shared structure: Bayesian odds multiply by likelihood ratios. Logarithms turn these ratios into additive evidence, and expectation of a log-likelihood ratio produces KL divergence under the generating law.
Limits: Evidence factors multiply separately only with the appropriate conditional-independence factorization. A favorable likelihood ratio is not a guarantee that a hypothesis is true, and a chosen alternative affects the comparison.
Transfer question: Which ratios are being multiplied in your problem, and what would their logarithms make additive?
Patterns: Exponentials and logarithms; Information and uncertainty; Decomposition

Title: Unpacking nested boxes
Mental picture: A delivery arrives in a box inside another box. Learning the outer label removes one kind of uncertainty; opening the inner box resolves what remains.
Shared structure: Chain rules decompose joint uncertainty or divergence into a marginal term and a conditional term averaged over the first variable. The same conditioning operation decomposes variance into between-group and within-group components.
Limits: Entropy, KL and variance have different units and algebra; their decompositions are structurally related but their terms cannot be exchanged. Conditional terms must be weighted by the correct conditioning law.
Transfer question: What becomes simpler if you first group outcomes by an intermediate variable?

Title: Postage priced by surprise
Mental picture: A postal system gives common messages short labels and rare messages longer labels. Over many deliveries, the average label length becomes more relevant than the longest individual label.
Shared structure: A probability law suggests ideal length proportional to negative log probability. Prefix constraints restrict feasible code lengths, entropy lower-bounds their mean, and typical-set coding approaches the entropy rate in repeated sources.
Limits: Real prefix code lengths are integer numbers of symbols and have overhead. The asymptotic statement needs its source assumptions; an arbitrary sequence has no automatically applicable probability model.
Transfer question: Which outcomes dominate the average cost: common inexpensive ones or rare expensive ones?
Patterns: Information and uncertainty; Averaging; Exponentials and logarithms

Title: Ink spreading on paper
Mental picture: Imagine a probability density drawn as ink that is gradually blurred by a Gaussian kernel. Sharp variations smooth out as the blur scale grows.
Shared structure: Adding independent Gaussian noise evolves a density by the heat equation. De Bruijn's identity measures the entropy increase using the spatial Fisher information, the squared gradient of log density averaged under that density.
Limits: Higher entropy here means broader probabilistic uncertainty, not improved image quality. Spatial and parameter Fisher information must not be confused, and the derivative identity requires the stated regularity or Gaussian-smoothing conditions.
Transfer question: Can a difficult static quantity be understood by watching how it changes under a simple smoothing operation?
Patterns: Local linearization; Information and uncertainty; Limits and convergence

Title: Water allocated above uneven floors
Mental picture: Several narrow tanks have floors at different heights. Pour a fixed amount of water so that the usable tanks share a common water level; tanks with very high floors stay dry.
Shared structure: For parallel Gaussian channels, maximizing a concave sum of logarithmic capacities under a power budget equalizes the marginal gain on active channels. Noise levels play the role of floor heights.
Limits: The tank geometry is a visualization of separable logarithmic optimization. Coupled interference, unequal channel scalings or discrete transmission constraints change the allocation problem and may change the formula.
Transfer question: Which resources should have equal marginal benefit at an optimum, and which should receive none?

Title: Tolls that certify an impossible route
Mental picture: Suppose a shipment must obey several route constraints. Someone assigns tolls to the constraints so that every allowed movement has a nonnegative toll, yet the required delivery would have a negative toll.
Shared structure: A separating linear functional certifies infeasibility. Farkas' lemma states the precise alternative between a nonnegative solution to Ax=b and a vector whose inner products rule out every such solution.
Limits: Tolls can be signed mathematical multipliers rather than actual money. The certificate applies to the stated linear cone; nonlinear or integer constraints can require different certificates.
Transfer question: Can you prove that a target is impossible by finding one quantity that every allowed construction must respect?

Title: A fence that yields a little
Mental picture: A rigid fence permits only positions inside a region. Replacing it with a springy fence lets a position move toward feasibility while balancing how far it travels.
Shared structure: An indicator of a convex set encodes a hard constraint. A proximal step minimizes a function plus squared displacement, and a Moreau envelope records the best compromise as a smooth value function.
Limits: The Moreau envelope is a value function, not the same object as the proximal point. A physical spring picture relies on Euclidean quadratic cost; nonconvex functions can give nonunique proximal choices.
Transfer question: Could a hard or nonsmooth requirement become easier by solving a small distance-penalized subproblem?

Title: Unseen directions in a room
Mental picture: Sensors in a room observe only certain directions. Moving an object in a direction invisible to every sensor cannot improve the measurements, so a size penalty discourages that movement.
Shared structure: In a reproducing-kernel Hilbert space, evaluation at training points is an inner product with kernel sections. Any component orthogonal to their span leaves training predictions unchanged while increasing a strictly increasing norm penalty.
Limits: The room is an abstract function space and the sensors are evaluations, not necessarily physical directions. The conclusion depends on the loss using only those evaluations and on the form of the norm penalty.
Transfer question: Which directions of your model cannot change anything the objective observes?

Title: Different rulers for the same change
Mental picture: Two mapmakers draw the same landscape using different coordinates. A one-centimeter move on one map need not represent the same physical change as a one-centimeter move on the other.
Shared structure: Parameter displacement and distributional displacement are different. Fisher information gives the local quadratic KL change, and its inverse converts a coordinate gradient into a natural-gradient direction.
Limits: Fisher information must be nonsingular for an ordinary inverse. Natural-gradient direction is invariant under smooth reparameterization, but a finite Euler update in coordinates is not automatically exactly invariant.
Transfer question: What notion of distance captures a meaningful change in your model rather than a change of notation?
Patterns: Change of coordinates; Geometry and distance; Local linearization

Title: A local map of curved terrain
Mental picture: A hiker uses a small curved map of the ground nearby to choose the next step. If the map is unreliable far away, the hiker limits the step to a trusted region.
Shared structure: A quadratic local model uses gradient and curvature. Newton uses the Hessian, BFGS updates a curvature approximation from observed changes, and trust-region methods constrain the model's range of use.
Limits: An optimization objective is not literal terrain, and a stationary quadratic-model point need not descend when curvature is indefinite. Local approximation quality and step acceptance determine whether the method makes progress.
Transfer question: What observations tell you that a local approximation remains trustworthy at the step size you propose?

Title: A ledger of daily choices
Mental picture: Each day a buyer chooses an option before seeing that day's costs. At the end, the buyer compares the total bill with the best single option that could have been used every day.
Shared structure: Online regret compares a sequence of decisions with a fixed hindsight comparator. Projected gradient updates balance responsiveness to current gradients against movement within a feasible set.
Limits: Low regret against a fixed comparator does not promise the best action on every day or performance against an arbitrarily changing comparator. The bound depends on convex losses, bounded gradients and the stated feedback order.
Transfer question: Are you judging a changing decision process against a fixed policy or a changing ideal policy?

Title: How a shuffled deck forgets
Mental picture: Start with a recognizable deck order and repeatedly apply a random shuffle rule. Ask how many steps pass before the initial arrangement is hard to detect from the resulting distribution.
Shared structure: A transition matrix transports probability laws. Total variation measures the largest event-probability difference, mixing time specifies a tolerance, and spectral information can bound the decay in a reversible finite chain.
Limits: A shuffle rule can be reducible or periodic and fail to forget. The stationary distribution need not be uniform unless the rule preserves it, and mixing is a property of distributions rather than every single shuffled deck.
Transfer question: Which features of an initial state disappear quickly, and which persist as slowly decaying modes?
Patterns: Limits and convergence; Randomness and distribution; Decomposition

Title: Balanced traffic on a road network
Mental picture: Imagine towns exchanging travelers. One way to keep each town's population stable is to balance traffic separately on every road in both directions.
Shared structure: Detailed balance equates stationary probability flow along each pair of transitions. Summing these pairwise equalities gives stationarity, and Metropolis–Hastings constructs an acceptance rule that enforces them.
Limits: Pairwise balance is sufficient for stationarity but not necessary: steady circulation can preserve populations without reversing every road's flow. Achieving balance also does not by itself guarantee rapid mixing.
Transfer question: Can you construct a complicated invariant distribution by enforcing a simpler local balance rule?
Patterns: Conservation and balance; Symmetry and invariance; Recursion and iteration

Title: Two walkers sharing randomness
Mental picture: Two walkers start in different places but agree to coordinate their random moves. Once they meet, they can use identical moves and stay together.
Shared structure: A coupling chooses a joint law with prescribed marginals. The chance that coupled states differ bounds total variation, and a coalescent Markov coupling turns meeting-time estimates into convergence estimates.
Limits: The walkers are an artificial joint construction, not two independent experiments. A poorly chosen coupling may almost never meet even when the marginal chains mix quickly.
Transfer question: Can you compare two random objects more easily by placing them on one probability space?
Patterns: Randomness and distribution; Limits and convergence

Title: The accountant and the surprises
Mental picture: An accountant splits each change in a balance into what was predictable yesterday and what arrived as a surprise. The surprise ledger has no predictable average gain at the next step.
Shared structure: Doob decomposition separates an integrable adapted process into a predictable accumulated component and a martingale. Conditional expectation determines the predictable one-step increments.
Limits: Unpredictable here means zero conditional mean relative to a specified filtration; it does not imply independence or symmetry. A martingale can fluctuate dramatically and does not guarantee a safe stopping strategy.
Transfer question: Which part of a time series remains after removing everything its current information can predict in mean?

Title: An odometer for rough motion
Mental picture: A very jittery traveler can move back and forth so much that signed displacement hides the activity. An unusual odometer records squared small moves instead of absolute distance.
Shared structure: Brownian increments are of order square root of elapsed time, so sums of squared increments converge to elapsed time. This quadratic variation produces the extra second-order term in stochastic calculus.
Limits: Quadratic variation is neither ordinary distance nor classical kinetic energy. The notation (dB)²=dt summarizes a limit theorem and must not be manipulated as ordinary pointwise differentials.
Transfer question: What order of small increments survives when many tiny changes are accumulated?
Patterns: Scaling and homogeneity; Quadratic structure; Accumulation

Title: Giving the same paths new ticket weights
Mental picture: Imagine a catalog of possible journeys, with a number of lottery tickets attached to each journey. Reweighting the tickets changes which journeys are likely without redrawing the catalog.
Shared structure: A Radon–Nikodym derivative changes a probability measure. Importance sampling adjusts expectations by likelihood weights; Girsanov uses an exponential path weight to change Brownian drift on a fixed time horizon.
Limits: Individual continuous paths usually have probability zero, so tickets are a density picture rather than literal path counts. Absolute continuity and integrability conditions are essential; a local martingale weight can fail to have mean1.
Transfer question: Could a hard random problem become simpler under a different law whose likelihood ratio you can track?
Patterns: Change of coordinates; Randomness and distribution; Exponentials and logarithms

Title: A family tree asking about its future
Mental picture: A family survives only if at least one child's line survives. Each child faces the same future question that the parent faced.
Shared structure: Independent identically distributed offspring reproduce the same branching structure. Conditioning on offspring count gives the fixed-point equation for extinction and a simple recursion for expected population size.
Limits: The basic model assumes independent reproduction with an unchanged offspring law and no resource limit. Extinction probability is not determined by mean growth alone in every degenerate case, and expected growth is not typical path growth.
Transfer question: Does each subproblem reproduce the structure of the whole problem after conditioning on the first step?
Patterns: Fixed points; Recursion and iteration; Randomness and distribution

Title: A budget for rare alarms
Mental picture: A monitoring system schedules infinitely many checks, each with a small chance of sounding a false alarm. If the total expected alarm budget is finite, only finitely many alarms occur almost surely.
Shared structure: Summing event probabilities controls expected counts and tail unions. The first Borel–Cantelli lemma needs no independence; the converse for divergent sums requires an additional condition such as independence.
Limits: Small individual probabilities alone are insufficient; their sum matters. Strongly dependent alarms can all occur together, so the divergent-sum conclusion cannot discard its independence hypothesis.
Transfer question: Can you turn repeated random failures into a summable sequence of probability bounds?
Patterns: Accumulation; Randomness and distribution; Limits and convergence

Title: A wall of alarm panels
Mental picture: Testing one alarm is easy; watching a wall of thousands makes some false alarms likely. You can budget for any false alarm at all, or control the average fraction of false alarms among those you report.
Shared structure: Family-wise error and false discovery rate answer different questions. Bonferroni divides an overall error budget among tests; Benjamini–Hochberg compares ordered p-values with rank-dependent thresholds under its dependence conditions.
Limits: False discovery rate is an expectation of a random fraction, not the probability that every report is correct. Benjamini–Hochberg needs its stated independence or positive-dependence assumptions, unlike the basic Bonferroni bound.
Transfer question: Which error does your application actually need to control: any false claim or the proportion among reported claims?

Title: A curve described by a menu of slopes
Mental picture: Instead of listing the height of a hill at every location, give a menu of slopes and the offsets needed for lines with those slopes to stay below it. Under convexity, the menu can recover the hill.
Shared structure: The convex conjugate records the greatest gap between a linear functional and a function. Fenchel–Young gives the supporting-line inequality, and biconjugation recovers a proper lower-semicontinuous convex function.
Limits: A nonconvex hill is generally replaced by its lower closed convex envelope under biconjugation. A slope can have several contact points or none, so this is not always an invertible correspondence between points and derivatives.
Transfer question: Would a problem be simpler if described by its responses to linear probes rather than by coordinates of individual points?

Title: Moving piles of earth
Mental picture: Two landscapes contain the same total amount of earth. Choose how much earth to send from every source pile to every destination, paying according to distance.
Shared structure: A transport coupling is a nonnegative joint mass allocation with fixed marginals. Wasserstein distance minimizes movement cost, dual Lipschitz functions certify cost, and entropic regularization gives a smoother transport table.
Limits: Mass may split across destinations, so a transport plan need not be a deterministic map. Entropic transport at positive regularization is a modified optimization problem, and ordinary KL divergence does not account for ground distance in the same way.
Transfer question: Do your distribution differences concern where probability mass is located, not only how much each label receives?

Title: Phone calls along a family tree
Mental picture: Each branch of a family tree sends a short report toward a relative. A report summarizes everything on that side of the tree that the relative needs for the current question.
Shared structure: On a tree factor graph, a message is a partial sum over variables in one separated subtree. Multiplication combines independent factors conditional on the boundary variable, and summation removes variables.
Limits: The messages are functions of a boundary variable, not single verbal opinions. On graphs with loops, the same local updates can recycle evidence and need not produce exact marginals or converge.
Transfer question: Can you cut your dependency structure so that a whole subproblem communicates through a small boundary?

Title: Reports traveling backward through a factory
Mental picture: A factory assembles an output through many intermediate stages. To learn how a small adjustment at each stage would affect the final quality score, sensitivity reports travel backward along the assembly route.
Shared structure: Reverse-mode differentiation composes local Jacobian transposes with downstream derivatives. Shared intermediate computations accumulate contributions from every path to the scalar objective.
Limits: Sensitivity to a variable is not a causal explanation of observed behavior. At nondifferentiable points a chosen derivative convention may be used, and floating-point gradients still depend on the actual computation.
Transfer question: If many intermediate variables influence one final scalar, can you reuse backward sensitivity information?

Title: Rotating backup crews
Mental picture: A crew practices with different members temporarily absent, encouraging the task to work under many partial teams. Present members receive a scale adjustment so their average contribution stays comparable.
Shared structure: Dropout multiplies activations by independent Bernoulli masks and rescales by keep probability. Expectation preserves each masked linear activation, while training optimizes an average over perturbed networks.
Limits: Preserving a layer's expected linear activation does not preserve the expected output of a nonlinear network. The regularization interpretation does not make dropout exactly equivalent to every penalty or to an exact ensemble average at inference.
Transfer question: Which parts of your method rely too strongly on one feature being present every time?

Title: Music through a moving window
Mental picture: Listen to a song through a window that reveals only a short time interval. Sliding the window shows when different pitches occur, but a very short snippet makes close pitches harder to distinguish.
Shared structure: The short-time Fourier transform compares a signal with translated, modulated windows. Time localization of the window trades against frequency localization through the uncertainty principle.
Limits: The analogy concerns mathematical time-frequency spread, not limits of human hearing. Overlapping windows do not create new independent observations, and a spectrogram can hide phase information.
Transfer question: Do you need to know which frequencies exist globally or when each one is present?
Patterns: Decomposition; Symmetry and invariance; Scaling and homogeneity

Title: A stencil at many zoom levels
Mental picture: Move a stencil across a drawing and try it at different sizes. A small stencil catches fine marks; a stretched stencil catches broader shapes.
Shared structure: Wavelet analysis uses translations and dilations of one template. Energy normalization permits meaningful comparison across scales, while Fourier scaling exchanges time width and frequency width.
Limits: A wavelet coefficient is signed or complex, not a literal overlap area. Reconstruction requires admissibility and appropriate normalization; an arbitrary family of resized pictures is not automatically a wavelet basis.
Transfer question: Does your signal contain similar shapes appearing at different locations and scales?
Patterns: Scaling and homogeneity; Geometry and distance; Decomposition

Title: A known shape hidden in static
Mental picture: You are trying to spot one familiar pattern in a noisy trace. Instead of judging every sample separately, lay the whole pattern over the trace and add the agreements.
Shared structure: A matched filter takes an inner product with a known signal template. Cauchy–Schwarz identifies the weights maximizing output signal-to-noise ratio under white noise; likelihood ratios give its detection interpretation under Gaussian noise.
Limits: A mismatched template or colored noise changes the optimum. Maximum linear SNR and optimal hypothesis testing are related under the stated Gaussian model, but are not interchangeable for arbitrary noise laws.
Transfer question: Which single direction in your data contains the signal you care about, and what covariance defines its noise?

Title: The symmetry blender
Mental picture: Put every rotated or permuted version of an object into a blender that averages rather than chops. Features that depend on which orientation you chose disappear.
Shared structure: Uniform averaging over a finite group is an idempotent operator onto the invariant vectors.
Limits: The metaphor applies to linear averaging with an invertible group order; it does not imply that averaging arbitrary geometric objects preserves their shape.
Transfer question: Which changes of viewpoint should leave the answer unchanged?
Patterns: Averaging; Symmetry and invariance; Fixed points

Title: Agreeing on a ruler
Mental picture: Different symmetry operations distort your chosen ruler. Average all the resulting rulers so no operation receives special treatment.
Shared structure: A finite group representation becomes orthogonal or unitary under an averaged positive-definite inner product.
Limits: The ruler is an inner product, not an average of coordinate axes; this averaging proof uses a finite group and positivity.
Transfer question: Could changing how you measure make an existing symmetry easier to see?
Patterns: Averaging; Geometry and distance; Change of coordinates

Title: The symmetry sound mixer
Mental picture: A recording can be separated into recognizable tones. A group action can likewise be separated into irreducible symmetry components, with character inner products reporting their amounts.
Shared structure: Orthogonal irreducible characters resolve a representation character into integer multiplicities.
Limits: For nonabelian groups, the underlying blocks can be multidimensional; a character is not the full matrix Fourier transform.
Transfer question: What are the smallest patterns that remain intact under every symmetry?

Title: Dictionaries that respect verbs
Mental picture: A dictionary is useful only if translating a sentence before or after an operation gives the same meaning. Mathematical translations are tested by this compatibility.
Shared structure: Intertwining and naturality require two routes through a diagram to agree.
Limits: Naturality need not be an invertible translation; a natural map can deliberately discard information.
Transfer question: Does your proposed correspondence preserve the operations, or only match the objects?
Patterns: Composition; Symmetry and invariance; Change of coordinates

Title: The universal adapter
Mental picture: Instead of manufacturing an adapter for every destination separately, build one standard connector through which all suitable adapters uniquely pass.
Shared structure: Universal properties determine an object through a unique factorization of maps.
Limits: The allowed adapters must preserve the specified structure; uniqueness holds relative to that category and does not compare arbitrary functions.
Transfer question: What mapping problem does the object solve for every possible target or source?

Title: The identity test bench
Mental picture: Imagine a machine whose responses to all compatible probes can be reconstructed from one carefully chosen self-test. The identity map is that self-test.
Shared structure: Yoneda reconstructs a natural transformation out of a representable functor from its value at the identity.
Limits: One arbitrary observation rarely identifies a machine. The reconstruction relies on responses satisfying naturality for every morphism.
Transfer question: Can compatibility force every case from the identity case?

Title: Joining records by a shared key
Mental picture: Two databases describe different aspects of the same event. Pair records only when their common identifier agrees.
Shared structure: A set pullback is the compatible subset of a Cartesian product; a fiber product generalizes this requirement.
Limits: Scheme fiber products retain algebraic multiplicity and nilpotents; they are richer than a simple join of point records.
Transfer question: What shared observation must two partial descriptions agree on?

Title: Sewing from matching patterns
Mental picture: Cloth panels can be sewn only when their instructions agree along the seams. Local mathematical descriptions similarly need explicit agreement on overlaps.
Shared structure: Sheaf gluing provides unique global sections; pushouts glue objects along common pieces.
Limits: Gluing spaces and gluing functions are different constructions. Agreement of functions is exact, not merely visual similarity near a seam.
Transfer question: Which overlap conditions are necessary before local solutions become global?

Title: Compressing labels without losing a task
Mental picture: Many labels distinguish things your next task cannot tell apart. Replace each indistinguishable family with one label, keeping exactly what the task can still observe.
Shared structure: Quotients identify an equivalence class, and universal quotient constructions retain all maps respecting those identifications.
Limits: Arbitrary identifications need not respect multiplication; normality or the appropriate compatibility condition is essential.
Transfer question: Which distinctions can every permitted observer safely ignore?

Title: Flattening nested packages
Mental picture: A parcel may contain parcels that contain items. Unpack once at each level or flatten the packaging first; the final contents should agree.
Shared structure: Monad associativity compares two ways to flatten three layers, and its unit laws handle singleton insertion.
Limits: A monad is not necessarily a collection container. The package picture illustrates the list example and the laws, not every possible monad’s objects.
Transfer question: Do different orders of interpreting nested structure give the same result?

Title: Moving a condition across the question
Mental picture: A question can sometimes be rephrased by moving a construction from what you supply to what you ask for. The answer set stays the same.
Shared structure: Adjunction gives a natural bijection between two Hom-sets with a construction on opposite sides.
Limits: This is a correspondence of mapping problems, not an inverse relationship between the two functors on all objects.
Transfer question: Can a difficult construction on the input side be replaced by a simpler one on the output side?

Title: Volume through intermediate windows
Mental picture: A composite transformation sends volume through many possible coordinate windows. Add each window’s signed contribution to recover the total.
Shared structure: Cauchy–Binet expands a composite determinant across maximal minors.
Limits: The pieces are algebraic projection contributions, not disjoint physical chunks; signs and squared terms depend on the chosen specialization.
Transfer question: Can a global volume be reconstructed from lower-dimensional coordinate measurements?

Title: A bank of direction filters
Mental picture: Build a filter that passes one spectral direction and mutes all the others. Combining these filters reconstructs the original signal and the operator acting on it.
Shared structure: Lagrange interpolation evaluated at a diagonalizable operator yields idempotent spectral projectors.
Limits: For a nonnormal diagonalizable operator the filters need not be orthogonal or reduce Euclidean length; defective operators require more than these simple formulas.
Transfer question: Can you construct a polynomial that keeps exactly one component?

Title: A smaller audition room
Mental picture: Choose the strongest direction in a room, then close off one coordinate. The best available choices become constrained between those from the larger room.
Shared structure: The min–max principle makes principal-submatrix eigenvalues interlace.
Limits: The ordered real comparison depends on a Hermitian matrix and a principal restriction; arbitrary row deletion or nonnormal spectra do not obey this statement.
Transfer question: How do optimal values change when the set of permitted directions shrinks?

Title: Two independent dials
Mental picture: A device has two settings that act on separate parts. Combining the parts pairs every state of one with every state of the other.
Shared structure: Tensor products pair basis states, while Kronecker sums add independent spectral contributions.
Limits: Independent additive actions require A⊗I+I⊗B; adding a coupling term generally destroys the pairwise-sum spectrum.
Transfer question: Is a large system assembled from independent factors, or are there genuine coupling terms?

Title: Prime toolkits and local workshops
Mental picture: A global arithmetic object can be inspected in workshops, one for each prime. Each workshop records only the divisibility scale associated with its own prime.
Shared structure: Valuations separate arithmetic into local exponents, with product formulas linking them globally.
Limits: A p-adic size reverses ordinary divisibility intuition: a high power of p is small. Workshops cannot be combined by ordinary real-distance intuition.
Transfer question: Which information becomes simpler when only one prime is visible?

Title: Restoring a number one digit at a time
Mental picture: A blurred digital display reveals one extra digit whenever you correct its current error. A nonzero modular slope tells you exactly which digit to choose next.
Shared structure: Hensel lifting solves a linear correction modulo p and builds a convergent p-adic root.
Limits: The digits are p-adic and the derivative must be a unit modulo p; a repeated modular root can split into several lifts or fail to lift.
Transfer question: Is the local slope invertible in the arithmetic system you are using?

Title: The receipt left by a carry
Mental picture: When digits overflow their column, a carry is a visible record that something crossed a base threshold. In a binomial coefficient, those records count prime factors.
Shared structure: Kummer converts a factorial valuation difference into the number of base-p carries; Lucas tests the zero-carry case modulo p.
Limits: Carries are counted in base p for prime p; arbitrary decimal carries do not measure a general prime valuation.
Transfer question: Could a divisibility question be read from digit behavior?

Title: Tuning an arithmetic radio
Mental picture: Different channels carry different residue-class signals. Mix the character channels with the right phases and only the selected class remains.
Shared structure: Character orthogonality on the unit group constructs an indicator for a reduced residue class.
Limits: These channels live on invertible residue classes under multiplication; they are not the ordinary additive Fourier frequencies on all residues.
Transfer question: Which symmetry group supplies the right frequencies for this filtering problem?

Title: Repairing a broken inventory
Mental picture: Individual items may admit incompatible unpacking lists. Keep an inventory of the collections they generate, where a unique prime inventory is restored.
Shared structure: Dedekind ideals factor uniquely even when elements fail unique factorization; the class group measures which ideals lack a single generator.
Limits: Ideals are sets closed under arithmetic operations, not arbitrary bags of factors. The class group does not count how many element factorizations a particular element has.
Transfer question: Would moving from individual elements to the structures they generate restore uniqueness?

Title: Rooms that repeat forever
Mental picture: Tile a floor with identical rooms. If a symmetric convex region is large enough, two appropriately chosen positions must differ by a room-to-room translation lying in the region.
Shared structure: Minkowski converts volume relative to a lattice cell into existence of a nonzero lattice point.
Limits: Large volume alone is insufficient: convexity and central symmetry enable the difference argument and set the 2^n threshold.
Transfer question: What is the correct fundamental cell for this continuous pigeonhole problem?

Title: Sorting into ordered tracks
Mental picture: Each item must go onto a track where all items are comparable. A collection of mutually incomparable items forces separate tracks, and remarkably that obstruction is sufficient.
Shared structure: Dilworth identifies poset width with the minimum chain-partition count.
Limits: A chain need not be a path between neighboring ranks; the track picture concerns comparability, not physical position or arrival time.
Transfer question: What is the largest set of items that cannot share one ordered track?

Title: Routes and blockades
Mental picture: To make transport robust, build several routes that share no internal junction. To stop every route, remove junctions; the two best numbers coincide.
Shared structure: Menger relates internally vertex-disjoint paths to separating vertex sets.
Limits: The chosen resource matters: edge-disjoint and vertex-disjoint routes are different, and the vertex statement excludes adjacent terminals.
Transfer question: Which scarce resource creates the bottleneck: edges, junctions, or something else?

Title: Tension in a network
Mental picture: Give every vertex a height and penalize neighboring vertices for disagreeing. A signal that is constant on one connected island creates no tension inside it.
Shared structure: Graph Dirichlet energy is a sum of weighted squared differences, whose zero modes are componentwise constants.
Limits: The heights are scalar values; no literal spatial spring layout is needed. Cheeger bounds use degree normalization and specific cut-volume conventions.
Transfer question: Where can a signal vary significantly while paying little edge energy?
Patterns: Quadratic structure; Decomposition; Boundary and interior

Title: The value of a detour
Mental picture: A connection is crucial when few alternate routes can replace it. Its electrical resistance measures this global scarcity better than its local weight alone.
Shared structure: An edge’s conductance times effective resistance is its spanning-tree inclusion probability.
Limits: Effective resistance combines routes through linear circuit laws, not by choosing just the shortest path; edge weights here are conductances.
Transfer question: Which edge appears local but has a globally irreplaceable role?

Title: An exchangeable team
Mental picture: Two teams each have enough independent skills to be complete. A suitable one-for-one exchange can preserve completeness in both teams.
Shared structure: Matroid symmetric basis exchange abstracts the exchange behavior of vector bases and spanning trees.
Limits: Not every real-world feasibility rule is a matroid; without the exchange axiom, a local trade may fail even when both teams are feasible.
Transfer question: Does your notion of independence actually satisfy an exchange rule?

Title: A dashboard with many settings
Mental picture: One dashboard records two kinds of defect for every candidate: missing connectivity and excess redundancy. Different dial settings reveal different familiar counts.
Shared structure: The Tutte polynomial packages rank deficit and nullity, and specializations recover coloring or basis counts.
Limits: Polynomial evaluation often cancels signed terms; it does not always filter subsets by simply retaining positive counts.
Transfer question: Can several apparently separate quantities be evaluations of one richer invariant?

Title: Maps at different zooms
Mental picture: A street map is almost flat around your feet, yet a whole journey can reveal curvature or loops. Local coordinates and global topology answer different questions.
Shared structure: Tangent linearization is local; global geometry requires completeness, curvature hypotheses and control of loops.
Limits: A tangent space is not generally a literal patch of the manifold; even a global exponential chart need not preserve Euclidean distances.
Transfer question: Which part of an argument is local, and what extra hypothesis makes it global?

Title: A fan of launched paths
Mental picture: Launch nearby paths from nearby directions. Their infinitesimal separation can oscillate or expand depending on curvature.
Shared structure: Jacobi fields are the linearized variations of geodesics, with the Riemann tensor supplying the coupling.
Limits: The picture describes infinitesimal variation, not arbitrary far-apart paths; geodesic parameters must be affine and sign conventions consistent.
Transfer question: What equation governs a small change in a solution, rather than the solution itself?

Title: A circulation that refuses to unwind
Mental picture: You can remove locally generated swirls from a field and still leave circulation around a hole. That remainder records the space rather than a local source.
Shared structure: Hodge decomposition separates exact, coexact and harmonic forms; harmonic representatives encode de Rham classes.
Limits: The clean decomposition assumes a compact oriented manifold without boundary; boundary conditions or noncompactness change the story.
Transfer question: Is a missing potential caused by a local equation or by a global hole?

Title: Complementary measuring sheets
Mental picture: In three dimensions, a direction can be paired with its perpendicular area sheet. The Hodge star extends this complementing operation to other degrees and dimensions.
Shared structure: Metric and orientation identify k-forms with complementary (n−k)-forms through the wedge pairing.
Limits: The picture depends on a positive-definite metric and orientation; dimensions other than three do not generally have the same vector cross product.
Transfer question: Which dimensions are complementary for the pairing you want to compute?

Title: Twisted local rulers
Mental picture: A ribbon can look ordinary in every small patch while a full trip reveals a twist. Bundles similarly carry global information that local coordinate descriptions can hide.
Shared structure: Characteristic classes detect obstructions to assembling local vector-space data into a globally trivial bundle.
Limits: Not every nontrivial bundle is detected by every listed class, and visual ribbon twisting is only a rank-one real example.
Transfer question: What can fail to line up after transporting local choices all the way around a loop?

Title: A place described by its observables
Mental picture: You can describe a place by its points or by every allowed measurement on those points. A map between places transforms measurements in the reverse direction.
Shared structure: Coordinate-ring duality replaces affine geometry by polynomial observables and contravariant algebra maps.
Limits: The observable class matters: polynomial functions encode affine algebraic geometry, not every feature visible to arbitrary set functions or distances.
Transfer question: Can you understand the object by understanding its permitted measurements?

Title: The first-order receipt
Mental picture: A complicated local object can issue a receipt listing only effects visible to first order. Extra lines on that receipt can reveal a singularity.
Shared structure: The cotangent quotient m/m² retains first-order functions; its dual is the Zariski tangent space.
Limits: A large tangent space is not the actual shape near a singularity; it forgets higher-order equations that may still strongly constrain points.
